drivingQuestion: In what condition and combination must ribs and vertebrae be damaged for the animal to be a tereifa rather than merely kosher or already a carcass?
outcomeNote: Every difficulty raised is answered: Rav's ruling is narrowed to a rib with half its vertebra, the clashes with ben Zakkai and R' Yoḥanan are distinguished by pestle-and-mortar, and Shmuel's contradiction is resolved by rib-without-vertebra versus vertebra-without-rib.

segments.he: אָמַר זְעֵירִי: וּמֵחֶצְיָין כְּלַפֵּי שִׁדְרָה. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּבִצְלָעוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן מוֹחַ.
segments.en: «Ze’eiri says: And» this applies only when the ribs were fractured «from the half of» the rib «toward the spine,» but not if they were fractured on the other half. «Rabba bar bar Ḥana says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: And» this applies only to fractures occurring «in large ribs that contain marrow;» fractures in small ribs do not render the animal a tereifa.

segments.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא, בֶּן זַכַּאי אָמַר: נֶעְקְרוּ – בְּרוֹב צַד אֶחָד, נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ – בְּרוֹב שְׁנֵי צְדָדִין. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בֵּין נֶעְקְרוּ בֵּין נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ – בְּרוֹב שְׁנֵי צְדָדִין.
segments.en: § «Ulla said» that «ben Zakkai says:» If the ribs were «dislocated» from the spine, even «a majority of one side,» i.e., six dislocated ribs, is enough to render the animal a tereifa. Only if the ribs were «broken» is «a majority of both sides» necessary. «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Whether they were dislocated or broken,» the animal is a tereifa only «with a majority of both sides.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַב: נֶעֶקְרָה צֵלָע וְחוּלְיָא עִמָּהּ – טְרֵפָה. אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב: נֶעֶקְרָה צֵלָע מִכָּאן וְצֵלָע מִכָּאן, וְחוּלְיָא קַיֶּימֶת, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: גִּיסְטְרָא קָאָמְרִיתוּ?!
segments.en: «Rav says:» If «a rib was dislocated and» the attached «vertebra» was torn out «with it,» the animal is «a tereifa,» even if the spinal cord remains intact. «Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:» If «a rib was dislocated from here and» another «rib from there,» i.e., both ribs connected to a single vertebra were dislocated, «but» the «vertebra» itself remains «intact, what is» the halakha? Rav «said to them: Are you saying» that an animal that was «sliced» in half is a tereifa? This animal is considered to have been sliced and already has the status of a carcass, as it is already considered dead (see 21a).

segments.he: וְהָא רַב נָמֵי גִּיסְטְרָא קָאָמַר? כִּי קָאָמַר רַב – צֵלָע בְּלֹא חוּלְיָא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But didn’t Rav also say» that «a sliced» animal is a tereifa, since he said that if a rib was dislocated along with the attached vertebra, the animal is a tereifa? In such a case, the opposite rib is inevitably detached. If so, the animal should be considered a carcass. The Gemara responds: «When Rav said» that such an animal is a tereifa, he was referring to a case where the «rib» was dislocated «without the vertebra.»

segments.he: וְהָא צֵלָע וְחוּלְיָא קָאָמַר? צֵלָע וַחֲצִי חוּלְיָא.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But didn’t» Rav explicitly «say» his statement with regard to «a rib and vertebra» that were dislocated? The Gemara responds: Rav meant that if «a rib and half» its attached «vertebra» were dislocated, the animal is a tereifa. The opposite rib, however, is intact and connected to the remainder of the vertebra.

segments.he: מִכְּלָל דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי, צֵלָע בְּלֹא חוּלְיָא אָמְרִי, וַאֲמַר לְהוּ: ״גִּיסְטְרָא קָאָמְרִיתוּ״? וְהָאָמַר עוּלָּא: בֶּן זַכַּאי אָמַר: נֶעְקְרוּ – בְּרוֹב צַד אֶחָד, נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ – בְּרוֹב שְׁנֵי צְדָדִין.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: «By inference,» one may conclude «that Rav Kahana and Rav Asi stated» their question with regard to a less serious case, i.e., where «a rib» from each side was torn out «without» the «vertebra» being damaged at all. «And» yet, Rav «said to them: Are you saying» that an animal that was «sliced» in half is a tereifa? Rather, this animal is a carcass and is certainly prohibited. «And» how could Rav say this? «But didn’t Ulla say» that «ben Zakkai says:» If the ribs were «dislocated,» even «a majority of one side» is enough to render the animal a tereifa, while if the ribs were «broken, a majority of both sides» is necessary? If so, any animal with fewer than six dislocated ribs should be kosher, as long as the spine is undamaged.

segments.he: אָמַר לָךְ: הָתָם זֶה שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד זֶה, הָכָא זֶה כְּנֶגֶד זֶה.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: Rav could have «said to you: There,» where ben Zakkai says that six dislocated ribs on one side render the animal a tereifa, this is referring only to ribs «not» dislocated «one opposite the other. Here,» where Rav says that two dislocated ribs render the animal a carcass, this is referring to ribs dislocated «one opposite the other.»

segments.he: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּרוֹב שְׁנֵי צְדָדִין, וּבְרוֹב שְׁנֵי צְדָדִין אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָא קָיְימָא (חד) [חֲדָא] מִינַּיְיהוּ זֶה כְּנֶגֶד זֶה!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But doesn’t Rabbi Yoḥanan say» that the animal is a tereifa only if «a majority of both sides» was dislocated, «and in a majority of both sides, it is impossible that one of them is not situated opposite another?» Still, Rabbi Yoḥanan says that the animal is a tereifa and not a carcass.

segments.he: הָתָם – בּוּכְנָא בְּלָא אֲסִיתָא, הָכָא – בּוּכְנָא וַאֲסִיתָא.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «There,» Rabbi Yoḥanan is referring to a case where «the pestle,» i.e., the end of the rib, was torn out «without the mortar,» the socket of the vertebra in which it sits, leaving the spine completely intact. In such a case, the animal is a tereifa only if twelve ribs were dislocated, even though this necessarily includes one rib opposite another. «Here,» where Rav says that two dislocated ribs opposite one another render the animal a carcass, that is referring to a case where the «pestle and mortar» were torn out together, damaging the spine.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דְּרַב? לָא שְׁמִיעַ לְהוּ דְּרַב.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «If so,» why did Rav Kahana and Rav Asi ask anything of Rav? Their case in question «is» identical to the statement of «Rav.» If Rav says that the animal is a tereifa if a rib and part of its vertebra were dislocated, that should be the halakha all the more so if ribs opposite one another were dislocated in addition to part of the attached vertebra. The Gemara responds: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi «did not hear» that statement «of Rav.»

segments.he: וְלִיבְעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ כִּדְרַב? סָבְרִי: לִיבְעֵי מִינֵּיהּ חֲדָא דְּפָרֵישׁ לַן תַּרְתֵּי, דְּאִי בָּעֵינַן מִינֵּיהּ חֲדָא, הָנִיחָא אִי אֲמַר לַן ״טְרֵפָה״ – כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן תַּרְתֵּי, אִי אֲמַר לַן ״כְּשֵׁרָה״ – אַכַּתִּי תַּרְתֵּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לַן.
segments.en: The Gemara persists: «But» if so, «let them ask» about the simpler case of one dislocated rib, «like that» which «Rav» himself discussed. Why ask specifically about two ribs opposite one another? The Gemara responds: «They reasoned: Let us ask him one» question through «which he» will «explain to us two» different cases. «As, if we ask him» about only «one» dislocated rib, «this works out well if he says to us» that the animal is «a tereifa,» because we can infer that «all the more so» if «two» ribs opposite one another are dislocated, the animal is a tereifa. But «if he says to us» that it is «kosher, we» must «still ask» with regard to a case of «two» dislocated ribs.

segments.he: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי דְּקָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ תַּרְתֵּי, הָנִיחָא אִי אֲמַר לְהוּ ״כְּשֵׁרָה״ – כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן חֲדָא; וְאִי אֲמַר לְהוּ ״טְרֵפָה״, אַכַּתִּי חֲדָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «If that is so,» then «now, too, when they ask him» about «two» ribs, they may not receive an answer with regard to both cases. Granted, «this works out well if he says to them» that an animal with two dislocated ribs opposite one another is «kosher,» since they can infer that «all the more so» it is kosher if only «one» rib is dislocated. «But if he says to them» that it is «a tereifa, they» must «still ask» with regard to a case of only «one» dislocated rib.

segments.he: סָבְרִי: אִם כֵּן מִירְתָּח קָא רָתַח. חֲדָא טְרֵפָה, תַּרְתֵּי מִיבַּעְיָא?
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «They reasoned» that it is better to ask about a case where two ribs opposite one another were dislocated, because «if» it is «so» that Rav holds that the animal is a tereifa if even one rib is dislocated, then «he would become angry» and respond: If an animal with even «one» dislocated rib is «a tereifa, is» it «necessary» to ask about an animal with «two» dislocated ribs?

segments.he: וְהָא קָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ וְלָא רָתַח, כֵּיוָן דְּקָאָמַר לְהוּ ״גִּיסְטְרָא קָאָמְרִיתוּ״ – הַיְינוּ רִיתְחֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But they did say» this question «to him and he did not become angry,» despite the fact that he holds that even one dislocated rib renders the animal a tereifa. The Gemara responds: «When he said to them: Are you saying» that an animal that was «sliced» in half is a tereifa, «this is his anger.» Rav Kahana and Rav Asi understood from this response that an animal with two dislocated ribs opposite one another is a carcass, but an animal with one dislocated rib is a tereifa.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב מַתְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: נֶעֶקְרָה צֵלָע מֵעִיקָּרָהּ, וְגוּלְגּוֹלֶת שֶׁנֶּחְבְּסָה בְּרוּבָּה, וּבָשָׂר הַחוֹפֶה אֶת רוֹב הַכָּרֵס בְּרוּבּוֹ – טְרֵפָה.
segments.en: § «Rabba bar Rav Sheila says» that «Rav Mattana says» that «Shmuel says:» If «a rib was ripped from its root, or» if the «skull was crushed in its majority, or» if «the flesh that envelops the majority of the rumen» was damaged «in its majority,» the animal is «a tereifa.»

segments.he: נֶעֶקְרָה צֵלָע מֵעִיקָּרָהּ טְרֵפָה? וּרְמִינְהוּ:
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Did Shmuel really say that if «a rib was ripped from its root,» the animal is «a tereifa? But raise a contradiction» from a mishna (Oholot 2:3):

segments.he: כַּמָּה חִסָּרוֹן בְּשִׁדְרָה? בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: שְׁתֵּי חוּלְיוֹת, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: חוּלְיָא אַחַת, וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְכֵן לִטְרֵפָה.
segments.en: «How much» is considered «a deficiency in the spine» of a corpse so that it will not be considered a full corpse that would render one impure in a tent? «Beit Shammai say: Two» missing «vertebrae, and Beit Hillel say: One vertebra. And Rav Yehuda says» that «Shmuel says: And» just as Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree with regard to ritual impurity, «so too» they disagree with regard «to a tereifa,» i.e., according to Beit Hillel an animal missing only one vertebra is a tereifa. Evidently, Shmuel holds that a missing vertebra renders the animal a tereifa, but a dislocated rib does not.

segments.he: הָכָא – צֵלָע בְּלֹא חוּלְיָא, הָתָם – חוּלְיָא בְּלֹא צֵלָע.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: This is not difficult. «Here,» where Shmuel says that a rib ripped from its root renders the animal a tereifa, he is referring to a case where the «rib» was torn out «without the vertebra. There,» where he says that a missing vertebra renders the animal a tereifa according to Beit Hillel, he is referring to a case where the «vertebra» was missing «without» the «rib» being dislocated. But if the rib itself was ripped from its root, the animal is a tereifa.

segments.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא צֵלָע בְּלֹא חוּלְיָא – מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, אֶלָּא חוּלְיָא בְּלֹא צֵלָע – הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? בְּשִׁילְהֵי כַּפְלֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Granted,» with regard to a case where «a rib» was dislocated «without the vertebra, you find this» commonly. «But how can you find» a case of a missing «vertebra without» a dislocated «rib?» The Gemara responds: This can occur «at the ends of the flanks,» where there are vertebrae with no ribs attached to them.

segments.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: וְלִתְנְיַיהּ גַּבֵּי קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל? אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב: כִּי אִיתְּשִׁיל – לְעִנְיַן טוּמְאָה אִיתְּשִׁיל, דְּהָווּ לְהוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְחוּמְרָא.
segments.en: Shmuel said that just as Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel disagree with regard to ritual impurity, so too they disagree with regard to a tereifa. «Rav Oshaya objects to this» statement: «But» if that is so, then the opinion of Beit Hillel is the more stringent one, as they hold that even one missing vertebra renders the animal a tereifa. Accordingly, «let» the tanna «teach» this dispute «along with» the list of «leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel» in tractate Eduyyot. «Rav said to him: When» the question «was asked, it was asked with regard to» the «ritual impurity» of a corpse. That is the source of the dispute between Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai, and on that matter, «Beit Shammai constitute» the «stringent» opinion. The parallel disagreement with regard to tereifot is not mentioned explicitly in any mishna or baraita, and it was therefore omitted from the list in tractate Eduyyot.

moves.cueHe: אמר זעירי: ומחציין כלפי שדרה
moves.summary: qualifies the baraita's count: only fractures from the rib's midpoint toward the spine
moves.about: which part of a rib must be fractured for it to count toward the majority — only from the midpoint toward the spine

moves.cueHe: אמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: reports R' Yoḥanan's further qualification that only large marrow-bearing ribs count
moves.about: reporting R' Yoḥanan's qualification that only large ribs containing marrow are counted

moves.cueHe: אמר עולא, בן זכאי אמר
moves.summary: reports ben Zakkai distinguishing dislocated ribs (majority of one side) from fractured ribs (both sides)
moves.about: reporting ben Zakkai's distinction between dislocated and fractured ribs

moves.cueHe: רבי יוחנן אמר: בין נעקרו בין נשתברו
moves.summary: holds that dislocation and fracture alike require a majority of both sides
moves.about: whether dislocated ribs render an animal a tereifa with a majority of one side only, or whether dislocation like fracture requires a majority of both sides

moves.cueHe: אמר רב: נעקרה צלע וחוליא עמה – טרפה
moves.summary: rules that a rib dislocated together with its vertebra makes the animal a tereifa
moves.about: the case they posit is not a question of tereifa at all — such an animal is sliced through and already has the status of a carcass

moves.cueHe: אמרי ליה רב כהנא ורב אסי לרב
moves.summary: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi ask Rav about ribs dislocated on both sides of an intact vertebra
moves.about: whether an animal is a tereifa when a rib on each side of a single vertebra was dislocated but the vertebra itself is intact

moves.cueHe: אמר להו: גיסטרא קאמריתו
moves.summary: Rav retorts that such an animal is sliced through and already a carcass, not a tereifa question
moves.about: the case they posit is not a question of tereifa at all — such an animal is sliced through and already has the status of a carcass

moves.cueHe: והא רב נמי גיסטרא קאמר
moves.summary: objects that Rav's own ruling is itself a case of a sliced animal
moves.about: Rav's own ruling — a rib dislocated together with its vertebra — is itself a case of a sliced animal, so he cannot dismiss their question as such

moves.cueHe: כי קאמר רב – צלע בלא חוליא
moves.summary: narrows Rav's ruling to a rib dislocated without its vertebra
moves.about: narrowing Rav's ruling to a rib dislocated without its vertebra, so that his ruling is not itself a case of a sliced animal

moves.cueHe: והא צלע וחוליא קאמר
moves.summary: objects that Rav explicitly said 'a rib and a vertebra'
moves.about: the narrowing just offered contradicts Rav's explicit wording, which said 'a rib and a vertebra'

moves.cueHe: צלע וחצי חוליא
moves.summary: re-reads Rav as meaning a rib with half its vertebra
moves.about: reading Rav's 'a rib and a vertebra' as a rib together with only half its vertebra, the opposite rib remaining attached

moves.cueHe: מכלל דרב כהנא ורב אסי
moves.summary: infers that the questioners' case was ribs dislocated with no vertebra at all
moves.about: that Rav Kahana and Rav Asi's question therefore concerned ribs dislocated without any vertebra at all, the lighter case

moves.cueHe: והאמר עולא, בן זכאי אמר
moves.summary: contrasts ben Zakkai, for whom fewer than six dislocated ribs leave the animal kosher
moves.about: ben Zakkai requires a majority of one side even for tereifa status, whereas Rav treats two dislocated ribs as making the animal an outright carcass

moves.cueHe: אמר לך: התם זה שלא כנגד זה
moves.summary: answers for Rav: ben Zakkai speaks of ribs not opposite one another
moves.about: ben Zakkai speaks of ribs not dislocated opposite one another, Rav of ribs dislocated one opposite the other

moves.cueHe: והאמר רבי יוחנן: ברוב שני צדדין
moves.summary: objects that R' Yoḥanan's majority of both sides must include opposing ribs and is still only a tereifa
moves.about: a majority of both sides necessarily includes one rib opposite another, yet R' Yoḥanan calls such an animal only a tereifa and not a carcass

moves.cueHe: התם – בוכנא בלא אסיתא
moves.summary: distinguishes the rib torn out alone from the rib torn out with its socket
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan speaks of the rib alone torn from its socket, Rav of the rib torn out together with the socket of the vertebra

moves.cueHe: אי הכי, היינו דרב
moves.summary: objects that on this reading the questioners' case is simply Rav's own ruling
moves.about: on that resolution, Rav Kahana and Rav Asi's case is identical to Rav's own ruling and there was nothing left for them to ask

moves.cueHe: לא שמיע להו דרב
moves.summary: answers that they had not heard Rav's ruling
moves.about: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi had not heard Rav's ruling, so the case was still open for them

moves.cueHe: וליבעו מיניה כדרב
moves.summary: objects that they should then have asked about the simpler single-rib case
moves.about: if they had not heard Rav's ruling they should have asked about the simpler case of a single dislocated rib

moves.cueHe: סברי: ליבעי מיניה חדא דפריש לן תרתי
